prompt: How does the Introduction describe man as a creature?

options.text: A unique creature possessing unusual endowments, with so much inside him
A fallen creature in need of restoration
A creature of habit shaped by his surroundings
The least of God's creatures but the most loved

explanation: 'Man is a unique creature, and possesses unusual endowments. There is so much inside man!' It leads straight into the claim that only eternity can reveal his total worth.

why.a: Correct. Unique, unusually endowed, and full of untapped capacity.
why.b: Wrong. The fall is discussed in Chapter 9 with Adam, but the Introduction's emphasis is on endowment.
why.c: Wrong. Environment shapes the mind in Chapter 7, but man is not defined that way here.
why.d: Wrong. Smallness is never the framing; the book is arguing the opposite.

prompt: What does the Introduction say the reader will have by the time they finish the book?

options.text: They will accept full responsibility for their life, and will have results to prove that God's Word is true
They will have memorised the key scriptures on the mind
They will know their calling with certainty
They will be free from every attack of the enemy

explanation: Two outcomes, and both matter: responsibility accepted, and results produced. It matches the book's whole claim that through the appropriate use of your mind you can produce the changes you desire.

why.a: Correct. Full responsibility and demonstrable results are the two promised.
why.b: Wrong. Memorisation is rejected later, where the author says he does not cram scriptures.
why.c: Wrong. Certainty about calling is never promised.
why.d: Wrong. Chapter 9 says every great door commands the attention of adversaries.

prompt: What does the passage say about the brain and reigning in life?

options.text: No one reigns in life without the use of the brain, and it is the effective use of the brain that secures you a throne on earth
Reigning in life is a gift of grace rather than a product of effort
Only those who reign over themselves can reign over anything else
Reigning belongs to the next life rather than this one

explanation: The throne image is used deliberately, and it sits with the neighbouring claims that every star in life is essentially sense-made and that supernatural intelligence calls for extreme attention.

why.a: Correct. Both halves are in the text, and the word is throne.
why.b: Wrong. The book grounds reigning in the USE of the brain, not in grace alone.
why.c: Wrong. Self-mastery is not a category this book uses.
why.d: Wrong. The throne is explicitly here on earth.

topic: keep thy heart with all diligence
prompt: How does the passage interpret "Keep thy heart with all diligence"?

options.text: As paying absolute attention to your mind, because your mind determines your ultimate worth in life
As guarding your emotions from being wounded
As keeping your motives pure before God
As protecting your health so you can serve longer

explanation: The book consistently reads heart as MIND in this verse, which is why Proverbs 4:23 heads a chapter called Understanding The Mind.

why.a: Correct. Absolute attention to the mind, on the ground that the mind determines your worth.
why.b: Wrong. Emotions are placed inside the mind by the book's own definition, but the verse is not read as protecting feelings.
why.c: Wrong. Motive is not the reading given.
why.d: Wrong. Health follows from the mind's use in this book, but that is not this interpretation.

prompt: What happens to the mind at new birth, according to the passage?

options.text: It is renewed and spirited, so that you are a new person belonging to a strange class
It is replaced by the Holy Spirit's own mind
It is cleansed of all previous learning
It remains as it was until the believer disciplines it

explanation: Renewal of the mind is named as one of the things that happen at new birth, Ephesians 4:23 is cited for being renewed in the spirit of your mind, and the phrase 'a strange class' is the author's own.

why.a: Correct. Renewed, spirited, and belonging to a strange class are all stated.
why.b: Wrong. You are given the mind of Christ, but your own mind is regenerated rather than removed.
why.c: Wrong. No erasure of learning is described.
why.d: Wrong. Discipline is required to DEVELOP the gift in Chapter 8, but the renewal itself happens at new birth.

prompt: What does the passage call the great task before you?

options.text: To keep your mind alive through a consistent learning process, so you do not become outdated
To find the work God has assigned you
To guard your heart from every negative word
To build something that will outlast you

explanation: It follows directly from the claim that people start ageing from the mind, and it is why the reader is told to be conscious of the need to be current and open to learn.

why.a: Correct. Keeping the mind alive by consistent learning, so as not to become outdated.
why.b: Wrong. Calling is not framed as a task to discover in this book.
why.c: Wrong. Guarding the mind is taught in Chapter 2 under imagination, but it is not called the great task.
why.d: Wrong. Legacy is not the goal named here.

prompt: What questions does the passage tell you to reason within yourself before moving?

options.text: This is where I'm going, how do I get there? What does it take to get there? How prepared am I to get there?
Who will help me, and what will it cost them?
Is this God's will, and will it bring Him glory?
What have others done, and how did it turn out?

explanation: Destination, route, cost and readiness, in that order. They are the tower builder's questions from Luke 14:28 turned into a personal checklist.

why.a: Correct. These are the questions as printed, and readiness is the last of them.
why.b: Wrong. Helpers are not part of this checklist; counsel has its own chapter.
why.c: Wrong. Discerning God's will is not how the book frames the decision.
why.d: Wrong. Learning from others is Chapter 8's material, not these questions.

prompt: What does the quoted text say about Daniel's name?

options.text: That he is the same Daniel whom the king named Belshazzar
That his name meant God is my judge
That he refused any Babylonian name
That the queen alone still called him Daniel

explanation: A detail inside the Daniel 5:11-12 quotation, and a confusing one, because Belshazzar is also the name of the king in the same story. The king then tells Daniel directly that the spirit of the gods is in him.

why.a: Correct. The verse says the same Daniel whom the king named Belshazzar.
why.b: Wrong. The meaning of his name is never given in this book.
why.c: Wrong. Refusing a name is not part of the account; he refused to DEFILE himself, per Daniel 1:8.
why.d: Wrong. The queen names him but no such exclusivity is claimed.

prompt: What is supernatural empowerment for, according to the passage?

options.text: To enable you to fully represent Jesus, witnessing to His resurrection and representing His kingdom with colour, beauty, power and authority
To enable you to endure persecution without falling away
To equip you for a specific office in the church
To confirm to you personally that you are saved

explanation: Four qualities are named for how you represent the kingdom, and the scripture is glossed as 'You shall reflect and represent Me bodily. The Holy Ghost will empower you to operate in My class.'

why.a: Correct. Representation is the purpose, with colour, beauty, power and authority named.
why.b: Wrong. Endurance under persecution is never discussed in this book.
why.c: Wrong. Church office is not the frame; John 1:12's power to become sons of God is.
why.d: Wrong. Assurance is not the purpose given.

prompt: What does the passage conclude about the reach of empowerment?

options.text: It is not limited to one realm but covers all the realms of your existence, and mental empowerment guarantees supernatural placement on earth
It is chiefly for the spirit, with the soul and body benefiting indirectly
It reaches the body only in cases of sickness
It is renewed each time it is needed and otherwise dormant

explanation: Ephesians 4:4 grounds it, that there is one Spirit, and the same Spirit that raised Christ quickens your mortal body. Luke 11:13 then makes the Spirit something you can ask the Father for.

why.a: Correct. All realms, and mental empowerment specifically guaranteeing supernatural placement.
why.b: Wrong. The book insists the mind is as important as the spirit, so it does not rank them this way.
why.c: Wrong. The quickening of the mortal body is described as ongoing fresh health, not occasional.
why.d: Wrong. Dormancy is not how empowerment is described.

prompt: Which scripture is quoted for Christ becoming poor so that we might be rich?

options.text: 2 Corinthians 8:9
Philippians 2:7
Psalm 1:3
Matthew 11:19

explanation: 2 Corinthians 8:9 opens the prosperity worked example, which then runs through knowledge, understanding and wisdom in turn. It is paired with the observation that many know He took their infirmity yet are still sick.

why.a: Correct. 2 Corinthians 8:9 is the though he was rich verse.
why.b: Wrong. Philippians 2:7 on making himself of no reputation is not quoted in this book.
why.c: Wrong. Psalm 1:3 is quoted a page later, for whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.
why.d: Wrong. Matthew 11:19 is wisdom being justified of her children.

prompt: In which year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign did he dream the dreams that troubled him?

options.text: The second year
The third year
The first year
The seventh year

explanation: 'And in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, wherewith his spirit was troubled, and his sleep brake from him.' The phrase his sleep brake from him is the memorable part.

why.a: Correct. The second year, as the quoted verse states.
why.b: Wrong. The third year is a plausible near miss the text does not give.
why.c: Wrong. The first year is not what the verse says.
why.d: Wrong. Seven appears nowhere in this account.

prompt: What does the passage conclude by quoting Paul that this wisdom is not the wisdom of this world nor of the princes of this world?

options.text: That when put side by side divine wisdom, those other levels of wisdom equal zero
That worldly wisdom is useful but must be submitted to God
That the princes of this world will one day acknowledge it
That worldly wisdom belongs to an earlier dispensation

explanation: Cited to 1 Corinthians 2:6. The same arithmetic reappears in Chapter 6, where without the 1 per cent of inspiration the 99 per cent equals zero.

why.a: Correct. Equal zero is the phrase, and it is a comparison rather than a mere ranking.
why.b: Wrong. Submission of worldly wisdom is not the conclusion drawn.
why.c: Wrong. Future acknowledgment is not mentioned.
why.d: Wrong. Dispensations are never discussed in this book.

prompt: What does Daniel 1:17 say about the four children?

options.text: God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom, and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams
They purposed in their hearts not to defile themselves
They were found ten times better than all the magicians
They were taught the tongue of the Chaldeans

explanation: It is the proof text for GOD GIVES IT, the section arguing that the wisdom operating in Daniel had its source in God. Job 28:20 asks the same question: whence then cometh wisdom?

why.a: Correct. This is Daniel 1:17 as quoted, with Daniel's extra portion in visions and dreams.
why.b: Wrong. That is Daniel 1:8, cited in Chapters 4 and 9 for the fear of God.
why.c: Wrong. The ten times better verse is genuine but is not quoted in this book.
why.d: Wrong. Their education in Chaldean is not mentioned here.

prompt: What did divine wisdom cause Joseph to enjoy, according to the passage?

options.text: Upliftment, enlargement, peace, pleasantness and liberty
Riches, honour and long life
Favour, protection and increase
Insight, foresight and dominion

explanation: Five things, offered as evidence that divine wisdom commands practical proofs and is not rhetoric but practical.

why.a: Correct. These five are the ones named of Joseph.
why.b: Wrong. Riches, honour and length of days come from Proverbs 3 in Chapter 5.
why.c: Wrong. None of these three are used in this sentence.
why.d: Wrong. Insight, foresight and dominion belong to the treasure of wisdom in Chapter 10.

prompt: According to Job 28:28 as quoted, what is wisdom and what is understanding?

options.text: The fear of the Lord is wisdom, and to depart from evil is understanding
The knowledge of the holy is wisdom, and the fear of the Lord is understanding
To seek God is wisdom, and to obey Him is understanding
To love mercy is wisdom, and to walk humbly is understanding

explanation: The author's conclusion is that departing from evil is your only access to this wisdom. Meekness is added as a further requirement, on the ground that meekness is required to get anything from God.

why.a: Correct. Fear of the Lord as wisdom, departing from evil as understanding.
why.b: Wrong, and it is the trap, because 'the knowledge of the holy is understanding' IS a real phrase, from Proverbs 9:10, which the book also quotes. The pairing here is different.
why.c: Wrong. Seeking and obeying are not the terms this verse uses.
why.d: Wrong. That echoes Micah 6:8, which this book does not quote.

topic: let not the wise man glory
prompt: According to Jeremiah 9:23 as quoted, who is told not to glory, and in what?

options.text: The wise man in his wisdom, the mighty man in his might, and the rich man in his riches
The strong man in his strength and the young man in his youth
The learned man in his learning and the ruler in his authority
The proud man in his heart and the boaster in his tongue

explanation: Three men, three grounds of boasting, quoted under MEEKNESS. Chapter 7 quotes the sequel from verse 24: let him that glory, glory in this, that he knows me.

why.a: Correct. Wise, mighty and rich, each with his own boast, exactly as the verse lists them.
why.b: Wrong. Strength and youth are not the categories in this verse.
why.c: Wrong. Learning and authority are not what the verse names.
why.d: Wrong. Pride is discussed in Chapter 5, but this verse names three specific men.

prompt: Which two scriptures are quoted to prove that divine wisdom communicates creative virtues?

options.text: Proverbs 3:19 and Psalm 104:24
Genesis 1:1-3 and Job 28:10
Proverbs 3:13 and Proverbs 3:16
Isaiah 43:19 and Matthew 13:54

explanation: Proverbs 3:19 says the LORD by wisdom hath founded the earth, and Psalm 104:24 says in wisdom hast thou made them all. Both are quoted again in Chapter 6 for inspiration. The conclusion is that God's wisdom is behind the creation of the world.

why.a: Correct. These two are the proof texts for wisdom's creative virtue.
why.b: Wrong. Genesis 1:1-3 opens the section and Job 28:10 comes later, but neither is offered as the proof pair.
why.c: Wrong. Those two Proverbs verses belong to JOY and WEALTH later in the chapter.
why.d: Wrong. Isaiah 43:19 is the philosophy of divine wisdom and Matthew 13:54 belongs to exploits.

prompt: What results does the passage say divine wisdom produces that natural men cannot deny?

options.text: A peaceful family life, progressive business and outstanding finances
Miracles, healings and deliverances
Sound doctrine, clear teaching and settled convictions
Long life, riches and honour

explanation: Three ordinary, checkable domains. It matches Chapter 1's promise that every crisis in your family, business or finances will disappear.

why.a: Correct. Family, business and finances, the same three the book uses elsewhere.
why.b: Wrong. Those are the supernatural feats the Spirit energizes you for in Chapter 3.
why.c: Wrong. Doctrine and teaching are not offered as the visible proof.
why.d: Wrong. That trio comes from Proverbs 3 and appears under wealth in the same chapter.

prompt: Which scripture is quoted as "by me kings reign and princes decree justice"?

options.text: Proverbs 8:15
Proverbs 3:16
Isaiah 11:9
Matthew 8:16

explanation: Proverbs 8:15, quoted under AUTHORITY to show that divine wisdom carries command. Alongside it, Matthew 8:28-32 gives a level of wisdom that orders the devil out, and verse 26 has Jesus rebuking wind and storm into a great calm.

why.a: Correct. Proverbs 8:15 is the kings reign verse.
why.b: Wrong. Proverbs 3:16 is length of days in her right hand, riches and honour in her left, under wealth.
why.c: Wrong. Isaiah 11:9 is quoted under dominion, on not hurting nor destroying in all my holy mountain.
why.d: Wrong. Matthew 8:16 is casting out spirits with his word, quoted just before this verse.

prompt: What does the passage say the wisdom of God is able to destroy?

options.text: All hurts, evils, regrets, failures and defeats
All sickness, poverty and untimely death
All ignorance, error and confusion
All curses, enchantments and bewitchments

explanation: Five things, quoted under DOMINION alongside Isaiah 11:9. When this wisdom came upon Solomon, God gave him rest on every side, with no adversary or evil occurrence throughout his reign.

why.a: Correct. These five are the ones listed.
why.b: Wrong. A familiar trio from elsewhere that this list does not use.
why.c: Wrong. None of these three appear in this sentence.
why.d: Wrong, and it is a near miss, because curses and enchantments ARE said to have lost their hold, but in Chapter 9 and on a different basis.

prompt: What does the passage say about the doctors of law and Pharisees who sat around Jesus?

options.text: They could not match His wits, His answers were far above their realm, and He levelled out their questions without any stress
They refused to accept His answers though they could not refute them
They plotted against Him because of His wisdom
They eventually became His disciples

explanation: It closes the ANSWERS section, and the chapter ends with the reminder that God's wisdom is full of good fruits, so look out for it.

why.a: Correct. All three details are given, and 'they knew it wasn't coming from an ordinary source' follows.
why.b: Wrong. Refusal is not what the passage describes; inability to match Him is.
why.c: Wrong. Plots are not mentioned in this book.
why.d: Wrong. No conversion of theirs is described.

prompt: The passage traces Solomon's journey through three verses in 1 Kings. What does each show?

options.text: 3:3 the foundation of his relationship, 4:29 the benefit of it, and 5:4 the effect of the wisdom given him
3:3 his coronation, 4:29 his building works, and 5:4 his alliances
3:3 his dream at Gibeon, 4:29 his judgment between two women, and 5:4 his treaty with Hiram
3:3 his youth, 4:29 his prime, and 5:4 his old age

explanation: 1 Kings 3:3 is 'And Solomon loved the Lord', 4:29 is God giving him wisdom and largeness of heart as the sand on the sea shore, and 5:4 is rest on every side with neither adversary nor evil occurrent.

why.a: Correct. Foundation, benefit and effect are the three labels the author attaches.
why.b: Wrong. None of these are what the three verses are cited for.
why.c: Wrong. All three events are genuine in 1 Kings but are not what this passage quotes.
why.d: Wrong. His old age appears later, in 1 Kings 11, when his wives turned his heart.

prompt: What does the passage say God did when Solomon began to love many strange women instead of Him?

options.text: He got angry with him and withdrew His wisdom from him
He sent a prophet to warn him
He allowed him to continue until his death
He took the kingdom from him immediately

explanation: Withdrawal of wisdom is the specific act, and it is what makes Solomon the proof that wisdom can be lost. In the place of peace God then stirred up adversaries against him.

why.a: Correct. Anger and the withdrawal of wisdom, in that order.
why.b: Wrong. No prophet appears in this account.
why.c: Wrong. God acted, by withdrawing wisdom and raising adversaries.
why.d: Wrong. The division of the kingdom is not discussed in this book.

topic: who knows the things of God
prompt: Which scripture introduces the definition of inspiration?

options.text: 1 Corinthians 2:11, that the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God
1 Corinthians 2:16, that we have the mind of Christ
Job 28:28, that the fear of the Lord is wisdom
2 Timothy 3:16, that all scripture is given by inspiration

explanation: 1 Corinthians 2:11 sets up the definition by establishing that only God's Spirit knows God's things, which is why inspiration must be the Spirit in motion in your mental faculty.

why.a: Correct. It stands immediately before the definition and supplies its logic.
why.b: Wrong. 1 Corinthians 2:16 is the mind of Christ, quoted in Chapter 1.
why.c: Wrong. Job 28:28 belongs to Chapter 4 on the fear of God.
why.d: Wrong. 2 Timothy 3:16 comes LATER in this chapter, for how scripture was delivered.

prompt: What declaration does the chapter on inspiration give the reader to make?

options.text: "Spirit of God, begin to move inside me now. Move me out of every mental blockage, into the realms of mental enlargement"
"I am connected to the highest order of wisdom"
"Lord, I want to see these virtues find practical expression in my life"
"Holy Spirit, show up in this matter. There must be a way out"

explanation: It fits the chapter's definition exactly, since inspiration is the Spirit in MOTION. Isaiah 55:8 follows, that God's ways are higher than your ways, so it takes that movement to connect with the higher level.

why.a: Correct. This is the Chapter 6 declaration, and its verb is move.
why.b: Wrong. That is the Chapter 4 declaration about the highest order of wisdom.
why.c: Wrong. That is the prayer in Chapter 5, after the list of wisdom's products.
why.d: Wrong. That is what Chapter 10 tells you to say to the Holy Spirit at a crossroad.

prompt: Which scripture says "And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business"?

options.text: 1 Thessalonians 4:11
1 Peter 3:4
1 Thessalonians 2:10
Isaiah 30:21

explanation: 1 Thessalonians 4:11, quoted twice in the book: here under quietness, and again in Chapter 9 against comparison, where the point is doing your own business rather than watching others.

why.a: Correct. 1 Thessalonians 4:11 is the study to be quiet verse.
why.b: Wrong. 1 Peter 3:4 is the meek and quiet spirit of great price, quoted just before it.
why.c: Wrong. 1 Thessalonians 2:10 is Paul's holily and justly and unblamably, from Chapter 4.
why.d: Wrong. Isaiah 30:21 is hearing a voice behind you, cited later in the same section.

prompt: Which scripture heads the chapter on exercising the mind?

options.text: Hebrews 5:14, on those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil
Hebrews 6:12, on followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises
Proverbs 27:17, on iron sharpening iron
1 Corinthians 8:2, on the man who thinks he knows something

explanation: Hebrews 5:14 is the epigraph, and its phrase 'by reason of use' governs the chapter. The first line after it is simply: your senses can be exercised.

why.a: Correct. Hebrews 5:14 heads the chapter and is returned to at its close.
why.b: Wrong. Hebrews 6:12 is cited in Chapter 9, under sin.
why.c: Wrong. Proverbs 27:17 appears inside this chapter, under research, but not as the epigraph.
why.d: Wrong. 1 Corinthians 8:2 also appears inside the chapter, on not assuming knowledge.

prompt: What saying does the passage use against those who do nothing about their dreams?

options.text: "If wishes were horses, beggars would ride", because there are too many wishers in the Church
"Faith without works is dead"
"A dream without a plan is only a wish"
"Many are called but few are chosen"

explanation: It sits with the claim that no one succeeds by accident, and with Anthony Robbins as the counter example, who read 700 books and got where he is through committed studies.

why.a: Correct. The proverb is quoted as printed, applied to wishers in the Church.
why.b: Wrong. A real biblical line that this book does not quote.
why.c: Wrong. A modern saying that sounds apt but does not appear.
why.d: Wrong. Also a real saying the book does not use.

prompt: What else does Abraham Lincoln say, beyond his line about being old at 20 or 80?

options.text: That the greatest thing in life is to keep your mind young
That a man is only as good as his word
That character is what you are in the dark
That the best way to predict the future is to create it

explanation: It closes the research section, alongside T. L. Osborn's line: so to keep living, you must keep learning. The point about consultants coming by tape, book or in person follows soon after.

why.a: Correct. Keeping your mind young is the second Lincoln attribution in the book.
why.b: Wrong. A common saying not attributed to anyone here.
why.c: Wrong. A real quotation from elsewhere that this book does not use.
why.d: Wrong. Also a well-known line the book does not quote.

prompt: Which two scriptures ground the teaching on insight-expectant prayer?

options.text: Jeremiah 33:3 and James 1:5
Jeremiah 9:23 and James 3:15
Isaiah 41:21 and Luke 11:13
Daniel 2:30 and Romans 11:33

explanation: Jeremiah 33:3 promises great and mighty things which thou knowest not, and James 1:5 says you can ask for wisdom if you lack it. Prayer is the fourth of the four ways to exercise the mind.

why.a: Correct. These two carry the prayer section.
why.b: Wrong. Jeremiah 9:23 is on meekness in Chapter 4, and James 3:15 is the four kinds of wisdom.
why.c: Wrong. Isaiah 41:21 is strong reasons in Chapter 2, and Luke 11:13 is in Chapter 3.
why.d: Wrong. Daniel 2:30 is meekness and Romans 11:33 IS quoted nearby, but the grounding pair is Jeremiah 33:3 and James 1:5.

topic: the keys of life and death
prompt: What did God say to the author during the encounter over his daughter?

options.text: "I am He that was dead, and behold, I live forevermore, and it is in My hand that the keys of life and death are"
"I will never leave thee nor forsake thee"
"My grace is sufficient for thee"
"Fear not, for I am with thee"

explanation: The exchange continues, with the author asking whether the key of death could be in God's hand while He favours His enemy with it, and God answering 'Never!'

why.a: Correct. This is what came to him, and it is the ground of the exchange that followed.
why.b: Wrong. A real promise that this book does not quote here.
why.c: Wrong. Also genuine scripture, also not used at this point.
why.d: Wrong. Another familiar assurance the book does not quote in this account.

topic: the fear of God and mental excellence
prompt: What does the passage say it takes to walk in mental excellence?

options.text: The fear of God, which grants unlimited access into the deep things of God, so you must shun sin and embrace integrity
A disciplined routine of study and rest
The approval of those who have gone before you
A calling confirmed by the church

explanation: Proverbs 1:7 is quoted again here, and the blockade the enemy uses is named: giving you a good taste for perverseness, crookedness and sin, until the brain cells are paralysed and the man starts doing silly and crazy things.

why.a: Correct. The fear of God is the condition, with unlimited access as its benefit.
why.b: Wrong. Routine is not what this passage requires; moral condition is.
why.c: Wrong. Hebrews 6:12 says to FOLLOW such people, which is not the same as needing their approval.
why.d: Wrong. Ecclesiastical confirmation is never mentioned.

prompt: Which scripture is paraphrased as God saying He will set you up on high above all nations of the earth?

options.text: Deuteronomy 28:1
Proverbs 4:18
Isaiah 43:19
Micah 2:10

explanation: Deuteronomy 28:1, used against accepting the status quo, with the condition attached: if you come on line with Me and do what I tell you to do.

why.a: Correct. Deuteronomy 28:1 is the above all nations verse.
why.b: Wrong. Proverbs 4:18 is the path of the just shining more and more, quoted in the same section.
why.c: Wrong. Isaiah 43:19 is behold I will do a new thing, used against the trap of past failures.
why.d: Wrong. Micah 2:10 is arise ye and depart, used against the pride of past achievements.

prompt: What two things does God say in the Isaiah 43 verses quoted against dwelling on the past?

options.text: Remember ye not the former things, and Behold, I will do a new thing
Fear not, and I have redeemed thee
Come now let us reason together, and If ye be willing and obedient
Call unto me, and I will show thee great and mighty things

explanation: Verse 18 forbids remembering, verse 19 promises the new thing, and the author's inference is that if you will not forget the former things you are not likely to know the new things God is about to do.

why.a: Correct. Verses 18 and 19 in sequence, and they are meant to be read together.
why.b: Wrong. Those phrases come earlier in Isaiah 43 and are not quoted here.
why.c: Wrong. That is Isaiah 1:18-19, used in Chapter 2 on reasoning.
why.d: Wrong. That is Jeremiah 33:3, used in Chapter 8 on prayer.

prompt: What does the passage say about the rich fool?

options.text: He prided himself that he had laid up enough to eat and drink till his time on earth was over, but God proved such a person has no reason to be alive anymore
He gave nothing away and so lost everything
He built bigger barns instead of helping the poor
He trusted in riches rather than in God

explanation: He appears under the PRIDE OF PAST ACHIEVEMENTS, so the fault the book finds in him is having concluded he was done, not greed. It sits beside the reminder that the devil compares you with age mates who are farmers in the village or who have died.

why.a: Correct. Having laid up enough is the fault, and God's verdict is that such a person has no reason to be alive.
why.b: Wrong. Failure to give is the usual reading and is not the one made here.
why.c: Wrong. The barns are in the parable but the book does not use them.
why.d: Wrong. Misplaced trust is another common reading the book does not take.

prompt: Why does the final chapter say God is preparing you to be relevant in this new millennium?

options.text: Because Jesus is getting ready to return, and the Church is taking her place at the top
Because the world is growing darker and needs light
Because the old generation of leaders is passing away
Because knowledge is increasing faster than ever

explanation: Two reasons in one sentence, and the promise follows that from now on your generation will start searching for where you live.

why.a: Correct. The return of Jesus and the Church taking her place are the two reasons given.
why.b: Wrong. Darkness is not the framing used in this chapter.
why.c: Wrong. Succession is not discussed.
why.d: Wrong. Increase of knowledge is a familiar idea the book does not invoke here.
